analyst_view.overall: Early view: Estoril are bottom without a league win, sacked Vasco Matos in mid-October and have lost 1-3 to Moreirense and 0-4 to FC Porto since Sergio Raimundo took over, first as interim and now permanently. Santa Clara under Petit are among the league's surprise packages near the top, though they have lost two of their last five. The bans listed for Pedro Pacheco and Emanuel Moreira should be served before this game, which is a month away.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean slightly lower: Estoril have struggled to score all season and top scorer Yanis Begraoui has been injured, while Petit's Santa Clara are well organised and keeper Neneca was decisive in the 2-0 win at Maritimo. The main risk is Estoril's leaky defence, which has conceded seven in two league games under Raimundo.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Nothing in the news points clearly either way: Estoril at home should have more of the ball against a Santa Clara side happy to defend and counter, which fits the site's split. I stay close to the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards. A desperate bottom side at home against a physical, compact Petit team should keep the game scrappy, which supports a fair number of bookings. No referee is named yet, so I stay with the model for now.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.6 shots. I lean a little lower: Santa Clara tend to keep games tight away from home, and Estoril's attack has been short of ideas and of Begraoui. A new coach still settling his routines is another reason to expect a less open game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target. Estoril's poor finishing and Santa Clara's counter-attacking threat roughly balance out. I stay with the model until team news is known.
